pairs.question: Quaenam causa genas tibi Florentes lacrumis occupat et mouet Tam tristes querimonias? An furto pecus, an dente periit lupi? Sic ut dura parens tibi Pulsarit tenerum uerberibus latus, Quod tu nunc doleas, sub hac Dum pendent capreae rupe? quid ingemis? Quid suspiria pectore Imo lenta trahis, sola sub ilice hac?
pairs.answer: Nec mi dura parens latus Pulsauit, neque grex est numero meus Furto aut dente lupi minor.
pairs.derivation: Opening exchange of the dialogue poem 'Hospes et Chloe'. The whole Hospes speech is one extended question asking why Chloe weeps (lost flock? beating by her mother?); quoted verbatim as the question with the inline parenthetical verse-numbers (1),(5),(10) and the speaker label (HOSPES) stripped. Chloe's reply opens with the operative answer denying each cause (not her mother, not a flock diminished by wolf); the answer ends at the first full stop after 'minor.', cutting before 'Sed longe grauior causa animum quatit...' where she turns from answering to elaborating on the graver, hidden cause. Speaker label (CHLOE) and inline number (15) stripped.
